=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf has multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (terminal leaflet present, with lateral leaflets in pairs along rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 3 (each compound leaf has three leaflets: two lateral and one terminal)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflet pairs are attached along the rachis in alternating positions, not directly opposite)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly elliptical with rounded base and acute apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip of leaflets is pointed but not drawn out into a long tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base of leaflets is broadly rounded, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with secondary veins branching off on either side)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy with light reflection, likely due to waxy cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, connecting leaflet to rachis without elongation)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem is green, flexible, and lacks visible bark or woody texture)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is uniformly green, consistent with young herbaceous growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no visible pulvinus at leaflet or petiole bases)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: One leaflet shows two distinct holes, likely from physical damage or insect activity, but no other damage is visible. The seedling appears healthy overall with consistent leaf morphology. The pink tag is an artificial marker and not a plant feature. All images show the same individual from slightly different angles; leaflet arrangement and venation are consistent across views.
